prompt: Leave the voicemail Dad leaves after hearing about your promotion. He is very proud. He will not say that.
response:
(Sound of a throat clearing, maybe a little gruff, a two-second pause after the beep)

“Hey, kiddo. It’s your dad. I, uh… I just got off the phone with your mother. She told me the news about the job. The promotion.”

(A longer pause. You can hear him exhale slowly.)

“Now, your mom, she’s gonna call you and give you all the ‘we’re so prouds’ and the happy tears, and you deserve all of that. But I… I just wanted to call and tell you something else. I’ve been thinking about that old treehouse I tried to build you. Remember that? Thing was a total deathtrap. Half the nails were bent, the ladder was just a couple of two-by-fours I prayed wouldn’t snap. A real mess. But you… you climbed right up there with your little plastic hammer like you were ascending a throne. You looked out over that yard like you’d just conquered the whole world.”

(His voice gets a little tighter, but he powers through it.)

“The point is, I’ve been watching you hammer away at your life, building this career. And I’ve seen you take scrap wood and build palaces. I’ve seen you straighten your own bent nails. I’ve seen you climb. And now… look at you. Look at the view from up there. I couldn’t build you a treehouse worth a damn, but you went and built a skyscraper. On your own terms. With your own two hands.”

(You hear a firm, single nod, like he’s confirming something to himself.)
